city.name: Philosopher's Path
city.description: Kyoto's Philosopher's Path from open data: the canal walk under its cherries from Ginkaku-ji to Nanzen-ji, past Honen-in and Eikan-do to the brick aqueduct and the Keage incline, with measured heights from Project PLATEAU on GSI laser terrain.

tour.title: The Philosopher's Path from open data
tour.text: {buildings} buildings from OpenStreetMap, Overture Maps and Project PLATEAU, on GSI 5 m laser terrain under GSI aerial photographs. The path follows the Lake Biwa Canal's branch about 2 km along the foot of the Higashiyama hills, from Ginkaku-ji to Nanzen-ji.

tour.title: Ginkaku-ji
tour.text: The Silver Pavilion, Ashikaga Yoshimasa's retreat (1489), was never silvered. The path begins at the bridge below its approach.

tour.title: Along the canal
tour.text: The philosopher Nishida Kitaro walked here daily; the cherries were planted from 1922 by the painter Hashimoto Kansetsu and his wife. Early April turns the canal pink.

tour.title: Nanzen-ji and the aqueduct
tour.text: The Sanmon (1628) stands about 22 m high. Behind it the canal crosses the precinct on a brick aqueduct of 1888, Suirokaku.

tour.title: The Keage Incline
tour.text: From 1891 to 1948 boats rode cradles up and down 36 m on these rails between the canal's two levels. Today the rails are a walk under cherries.

shore.encoding: r: 128 + 2 x signed distance to the shoreline (m, water positive); g: sand; b: rock

trees.note: Species are not mapped; the mix is a guess from Kyoto's street-tree surveys and the temples' own guides. The Higashiyama hillsides above the path are a laurel forest with cedars, pines and maples. The path's own cherries (Kansetsu-zakura, first planted in 1922) are planted along both banks by city.py, every 4 to 5 m as photographs show them; the area round the path makes them and the mapped trees there cherries. The path is not lit at night, so no yozakura.
